title: Single-Machine Multi-Instance Network Namespace P2P Test

results.description: Gossip discovery finds the peer within 60s
results.details: Both nodes show peer discovery events (peer pubkey in logs, NotifyJoin, or member count > 1)

WireGuard tunnel proven operational: Stream connections from peer mesh IP 10.10.29.165 in Node A logs (TCP through WG tunnel); Stream connections from peer mesh IP 10.10.188.13 in Node B logs; Node B joined gossip cluster via seed (tunnel operational); Node A received NotifyJoin for peer at 10.10.29.165; Node B received NotifyJoin for peer at 10.10.188.13

results.description: Bidirectional data transfer works through the tunnel
results.details: Bidirectional mesh data transfer confirmed: B->A stream connections confirmed; A->B stream connections confirmed; push/pull sync completed; NotifyJoin on both sides; Web UI accessible (HTTP 200); Cross-namespace HTTP access (HTTP 200)

results.description: NAT hole-punch succeeds or relay fallback engages cleanly
results.details: NAT traversal activity detected (STUN/relay/hole-punch) with successful resolution

results.description: Graceful leave detection works (peer removed within 60s)
results.details: Node B detected Node A's departure within timeout

results.description: meshdesk status shows peer as connected within 30s of startup

caveats: Does not test multi-hop routing (only 2 instances)
Network namespace NAT is Linux netfilter, not carrier-grade NAT
No real latency or packet loss simulation
Gossip uses loopback bridge, not real WAN
Mesh IPs derived from pubkey first 2 bytes (10.10.x.y)
Static WireGuard peers pre-configured to bootstrap tunnel before gossip
